This suggests two columns corresponding to... nLC = 3000 and 4000. Hmm. With Emax ∈ {10, 20, 25} t. The two columns likely correspond to different nLC values (3000 vs 4000), possibly for different capacities. vmin = Emax/nLC: for nLC=3000, vmin = 100/3000 = 0.0333%Emax? Hmm, vmin in %Emax: vmin = 100%/nLC... 1/3000 = 0.0333%. But given 0.02%. And Y = Emax/vmin: 100%/0.02% = 5000. Yes! Y = Emax/vmin. So vmin = 0.02%Emax → Y = 5000. vmin = 0.0113%Emax → Y = 8850 (1/0.000113 = 8850). And nLC: 3000 vs 4000. Hmm, nLC ≤ vmin relationship: nLC = 100/vmin(%): 100/0.02 = 5000, not 3000. Hmm, nLC is the max number of load cell verification intervals: nLC ≤ 0.7*vmin? pLC*vmin: 0.7*5000 = 3500. Hmm, 3000 ≤ 3500. 0.7*8850 = 6195, 4000 ≤ 6195. OK.

So the two columns represent two characteristic sets (two variants): one with nLC=3000, vmin=0.02%Emax, Y=5000; another with nLC=4000, vmin=0.0113%Emax, Y=8850. These are likely for the different capacities, but we don't know which maps to which. The column structure is colspan=2 for most rows but two values for these three rows.
